pairs.title: Late lift to the ferry
pairs.version_a: Malik had a job interview on an island at ten o'clock, and the only ferry that could get him there in time left at eight. His friend Priya had promised to drive him to the ferry terminal. That morning she ignored her alarm, went back to sleep, and picked him up forty minutes late. She knew nothing else about the ferry that morning. They reached the terminal at half past eight. Malik missed his interview, and the job went to someone else. A terminal clerk later told them that the eight o'clock ferry had sailed on time that morning. If they had arrived when Priya promised, Malik would have been on it and reached his interview.
pairs.version_b: Malik had a job interview on an island at ten o'clock, and the only ferry that could get him there in time left at eight. His friend Priya had promised to drive him to the ferry terminal. That morning she ignored her alarm, went back to sleep, and picked him up forty minutes late. She knew nothing else about the ferry that morning. They reached the terminal at half past eight. Malik missed his interview, and the job went to someone else. A terminal clerk later told them that the eight o'clock ferry had been cancelled that morning. Even if they had arrived when Priya promised, Malik would have been stuck ashore and missed his interview.
pairs.intended_difference: In A the ferry sailed on time, so arriving as promised would have got Malik to the interview; in B the ferry was cancelled, so he would have missed it anyway.
pairs.judgment_question: How much is Priya responsible for Malik missing his interview?
pairs.comprehension_question: What happened to the eight o'clock ferry that morning?
pairs.prediction_rationale: When the interview would have been missed regardless, readers see Priya's lateness as careless but not what cost Malik the job, so responsibility ratings should drop by around two points.
pairs.originality_note: An everyday broken promise about a lift, with a cancelled ferry as the independent cause; not based on any published overdetermination vignette.

pairs.title: Skipped Friday backup
pairs.version_a: Oskar looks after the computers at a small accounting firm. One of his duties is to copy the office server onto the backup drive every Friday before he leaves. One Friday he wanted to catch an early train, skipped the backup and went home. He knew nothing else about the state of the equipment that day. Over the weekend the server's disk failed, and that week's client records were lost for good. A technician who examined the equipment afterwards found that the backup drive had been working normally that Friday. She concluded that a backup made that evening would have been readable, and the records would have been saved.
pairs.version_b: Oskar looks after the computers at a small accounting firm. One of his duties is to copy the office server onto the backup drive every Friday before he leaves. One Friday he wanted to catch an early train, skipped the backup and went home. He knew nothing else about the state of the equipment that day. Over the weekend the server's disk failed, and that week's client records were lost for good. A technician who examined the equipment afterwards found that the backup drive had been silently faulty that Friday. She concluded that a backup made that evening would have been unreadable, and the records would have been lost anyway.
pairs.intended_difference: In A the backup drive worked, so the skipped backup would have saved the records; in B the drive was faulty, so the records would have been lost even with the backup.
pairs.judgment_question: How much is Oskar responsible for the firm losing that week's client records?
pairs.comprehension_question: What did the technician find out about the backup drive?
pairs.option_a: It had been working normally that Friday
pairs.option_b: It had been silently faulty that Friday
pairs.option_c: It had been stolen over the weekend
pairs.prediction_rationale: Readers hold a person much less responsible for a loss that the neglected duty could not have prevented, even though the neglect itself is identical.
pairs.originality_note: An office data-loss case with a hidden equipment fault, invented for this task and unlike standard philosophical pre-emption examples.

pairs.title: Bicycle on the stairwell railing
pairs.version_a: An apartment building has a rule: nothing may be chained to the stairwell railings, because the stairs are narrow. Jonas, who had just moved in, read this rule in his welcome letter and remembered it. One evening he chained his bicycle to the railing on the second-floor landing, to save carrying it up to his flat. Later that night his neighbour Mrs Okoye came down the stairs with a full laundry basket, as residents do every day. The basket caught on the bicycle's handlebar, she lost her balance and fell down four steps. She sprained her wrist badly and could not work for three weeks.
pairs.version_b: An apartment building has a rule: nothing may be chained to the stairwell railings, because the stairs are narrow. Jonas, who had just moved in, was never told about this rule, and no notice mentioned it. One evening he chained his bicycle to the railing on the second-floor landing, to save carrying it up to his flat. Later that night his neighbour Mrs Okoye came down the stairs with a full laundry basket, as residents do every day. The basket caught on the bicycle's handlebar, she lost her balance and fell down four steps. She sprained her wrist badly and could not work for three weeks.
pairs.intended_difference: In A Jonas had read and remembered the rule against chaining things to the railings; in B he had never been told of it.
pairs.judgment_question: How much did Jonas cause Mrs Okoye's fall?
pairs.scale_label_1: Did not cause it at all
pairs.comprehension_question: What did Jonas know about the rule on stairwell railings?
pairs.option_a: He had read it in his welcome letter and remembered it
pairs.option_b: He had never been told about it
pairs.option_c: He had been given special permission to ignore it
pairs.prediction_rationale: The physical chain of events is identical, so causal ratings stay fairly high in both, but knowingly breaking the rule makes his act stand out more as the cause, shifting ratings by roughly a point.
pairs.originality_note: A residential stairwell accident with a new tenant, unlike the published pen-taking or computer-login norm-violation vignettes.

pairs.title: Draft saved in the Ready folder
pairs.version_a: A local news website has a rule: unfinished articles must never be saved in the folder named Ready, because the publishing program puts everything in that folder onto the website. Mina, a new reporter, was told about this rule in her training and remembered it. One evening she saved an unfinished article in the Ready folder, because it was the first folder that opened. At six the next morning the duty editor, Paulo, started the publishing program, as he does every day. The unfinished article went onto the website. It contained an unchecked claim that a named bakery had failed a hygiene inspection. The claim was false, and the bakery lost most of its customers that week.
pairs.version_b: A local news website has a rule: unfinished articles must never be saved in the folder named Ready, because the publishing program puts everything in that folder onto the website. Mina, a new reporter, was never told about this rule, and nothing on the screen mentioned it. One evening she saved an unfinished article in the Ready folder, because it was the first folder that opened. At six the next morning the duty editor, Paulo, started the publishing program, as he does every day. The unfinished article went onto the website. It contained an unchecked claim that a named bakery had failed a hygiene inspection. The claim was false, and the bakery lost most of its customers that week.
pairs.intended_difference: In A Mina had been told the rule about the Ready folder and remembered it; in B she had never been told and nothing indicated it.
pairs.judgment_question: How much did Mina cause the bakery to lose its customers?
pairs.scale_label_1: Did not cause it at all
pairs.comprehension_question: What did Mina know about the rule on the Ready folder?
pairs.option_a: She had been told about it in training and remembered it
pairs.option_b: She had never been told about it
pairs.option_c: She had written the rule herself
pairs.prediction_rationale: Readers treat a knowing rule-breaker as more of a cause than an uninformed one; when she was never told, some causal weight shifts to the newsroom's set-up, giving a difference of about one point.
pairs.originality_note: A newsroom publishing mishap with reputational harm to a third party, not a re-skin of any known causal-judgment experiment.

pairs.title: Dog let off the lead
pairs.version_a: Ravi was looking after his friend Selma's dog, Pip, for a weekend. Selma had asked him to keep Pip on the lead in the park, because Pip sometimes chases squirrels and the far side of the park borders a road. On Sunday Ravi wanted Pip to have a proper run and unclipped the lead, thinking the road was far enough away. After a few minutes Pip bolted after a squirrel, straight across the grass and out into the road. A van was passing at that moment and struck him. Pip's hind leg was broken in two places. He needed surgery and could not walk properly for three months.
pairs.version_b: Ravi was looking after his friend Selma's dog, Pip, for a weekend. Selma had asked him to keep Pip on the lead in the park, because Pip sometimes chases squirrels and the far side of the park borders a road. On Sunday Ravi wanted Pip to have a proper run and unclipped the lead, thinking the road was far enough away. After a few minutes Pip bolted after a squirrel, straight across the grass and out into the road. No vehicle was passing at that moment, and Pip came back unhurt when Ravi called. Ravi clipped the lead on again, and they finished their walk and went home as usual.
pairs.intended_difference: In A a van happened to be passing and broke the dog's leg; in B no vehicle happened to be passing and the dog returned unhurt.
pairs.judgment_question: How wrong was Ravi's choice to let Pip off the lead?
pairs.comprehension_question: What happened when Pip ran out into the road?
pairs.option_b: No vehicle was passing and he came back unhurt
pairs.prediction_rationale: The choice is identical, so most readers rate it similarly, but a seriously injured dog makes the same decision feel worse, giving a shift of somewhat under a point and a half.
pairs.originality_note: A pet-sitting case where the chance element is passing traffic, unlike the familiar drunk-driver or reckless-shooter luck cases.

pairs.title: Parcel left on the doorstep
pairs.version_a: Teodor delivers parcels. His company's rule is that when nobody answers the door, a parcel must go back to the depot. One afternoon nobody answered at Mrs Lindqvist's house. Teodor was running late, so he left her parcel on the doorstep, in view of the street. He knew that parcels left outside on that street were occasionally stolen, though most were not. Mrs Lindqvist got home two hours later. The parcel was gone; a passer-by had taken it from the doorstep. It held her new hearing aids, and she had to wait five weeks for replacements, hardly able to follow a conversation in that time.
pairs.version_b: Teodor delivers parcels. His company's rule is that when nobody answers the door, a parcel must go back to the depot. One afternoon nobody answered at Mrs Lindqvist's house. Teodor was running late, so he left her parcel on the doorstep, in view of the street. He knew that parcels left outside on that street were occasionally stolen, though most were not. Mrs Lindqvist got home two hours later. The parcel was there; nobody had touched it on the doorstep. It held her new hearing aids, and she put them in that same evening, able to follow every conversation from then on.
pairs.intended_difference: In A someone happened to steal the parcel before she got home, leaving her without hearing aids for five weeks; in B nobody touched it and she got it safely.
pairs.judgment_question: How wrong was Teodor's choice to leave the parcel on the doorstep?
pairs.comprehension_question: What did Mrs Lindqvist find when she got home?
pairs.option_a: The parcel had been taken from the doorstep
pairs.option_b: The parcel was still on the doorstep, untouched
pairs.option_c: A note saying the parcel was at the depot
pairs.prediction_rationale: Leaving a parcel out is a mild, common shortcut, so ratings have room to rise when it leads to a real hardship; I expect roughly a one-point gap.
pairs.originality_note: A mundane delivery shortcut whose outcome depends on a stranger's theft, not adapted from any standard moral-luck example.
